text:
niya: Quick alert 1: silica13b-int8 hybrid canary showing warmstart OOMs + slowgen p95 spikes after enabling kernel-level sparse matmul. Logs point at KV slab growth and memcpy stalls.

niya: sample log:
```
[2026-03-25T14:12:03Z] OOM allocating 1.04GiB for kv_cache shard=2
model=silica13b-int8 host=canary-hp-4 slot=2 prefetch=10 max_new_tokens=640
trace: kv_cache.rehydrate -> slab.grow -> memcpy -> OOM
```

ras: interesting. we flipped sparse matmul kernels yesterday + enabled prefetch=10 to try to amortize attention cost. frag + simultaneous slab allocations probably the culprit.

peggy: initial mitigation options: drop prefetch to 2, reduce max_new_tokens to 256 for canary, enable slab_compact_on_evict and soft_reserve, or temporarily revert the new kernel.

niya: I ran a short sim locally with hybrid-int8 + prefetch=2 + max_new_tokens=256 + microbatch=4. peak kv alloc down ~55%, p95 latency improved for short sessions but long rollups >2k tokens are truncated.

tomas: thanks. also want a quick quality check: did quantization+kernel change affect generation quality? we need to run the 800-prompt eval (coverage: short, mid, long) to detect any regressions.

peggy: ran a smoke eval on 200 short/mid prompts: no significant quality delta. long-rollup tests show more truncation when hitting the new max_new_tokens cap.

niya: rolling a canary patch now with defaults patch (prefetch=2, max_new_tokens=256, slab_compact_on_evict=true, soft_reserve=true). ops-bot starting rollout.

ops-bot: deploybot: Rolling update 6932109999 -> silica13b-int8 defaults patch started. dashboard: https://console.redwood/models/silica13b/canaries/6932109999

ras: follow-ups: add runtime gauges kv_alloc_peak, slab_frag_ratio, and kernel_sparse_fallback_count. Alert if kv_alloc_peak > 900MiB or slab_frag_ratio > 30%.

tomas: also schedule a targeted eval job for the long-rollup set and a quantization regression check (BLEU/ROUGE+exact match on a small QA set). link results back here.

peggy: A/B for 30m after rolling to 2/3 canaries: OOM v1=9.9% -> v2=0.8%. p95 latency v1=138ms -> v2=102ms. cost/request -3.2%. quality: short/mid no regression; long-rollup shows expected truncation at the cap.

niya: plan: keep patch in canary 24h, run long-rollup eval and quant regression. if OOM <1% and quality impact limited to >2k requests, promote. otherwise revert kernel or maintain highmem variant. ticket INFRA-3602 created. PR #1012.

ras: one more idea: implement route override based on estimated total tokens (history+requested). auto-route >2k to highmem pool with original defaults. reduces regressions while keeping cost/perf gains for typical traffic.

niya: agreed. I'll add routing rule to INFRA-3602 and ask infra to add metric active_prefetch_windows to help diagnose.

peggy: thanks team  will monitor and post eval artifacts here. :thumbsup:
